newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - US T-bonds poised to probe below 109-00.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - US T-bonds poised to probe below 109-00.

text.p: June U.S. Treasury bond futures set a course for the 108-00 handle Wednesday, trading down to a low of 109-03 at midday after various support levels gave way, technicians said.
June futures slid through 109-16 and last week's low of 109-12, paving the way for a test of 108-30, the May 8 low.

The contract could probe deeper to the downside, to 108-24 or 108-16, but from there would probably bounce back toward the top of its recent trading range, said Terence Gabriel, technical strategist for I.D.E.A. Inc.
June was recently trading down 18/32 at 109-09.

In the next week or so, bond futures appear destined to struggle in a choppy sideways pattern before new monthly economic indicators, including U.S. employment data in early June, arrive to help illuminate whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates in July, Gabriel said.
On Tuesday, Fed policymakers chose to leave the federal funds rate unchanged at 5.50 percent.
"The trend studies suggest the market probably has entered into a lateral countertrend phase," Gabriel said.

He said daily stochastics had fallen sharply from their overbought levels of early May, while other indicators that measure the strength of the directional trend are also declining. "We're working off the overbought excess by churning and retrenching," Gabriel said.
To revive the fledgling upturn that began in April, June bond futures would need to close above 110-06, the contract's 200-day moving average, Gabriel said.
Bruce Kamich, senior vice president at MCM Moneywatch, said with most technicians decidely bearish on bonds, he was inclined to take a contrarian view.
He said the market put in a bottom last month, when June futures traded down to 106-12.
Reinforcing this view is 40-week cycle analysis that predicted the April low, Kamich said. According to this theory, he said, this positive cycle should last through Labor Day in early September.
"Any available weakness through the end of the month I would use as a buy opportunity for bonds," Kamich said.

However, Gabriel cautioned that above the 200-day moving average lies Gann resistance at 110-19, the May 13 high of 110-22, and channel resistance at 111-03 from the larger downmove reaching back to early December.
"Everyone is convinced the Fed will raise rates in July, so without numbers to alter that view, it becomes very hard for the market to rally," he said.
